_source: Bench cell for the Rosie 1420 V1 robot definition on the bench-servo nine-motor bench: six bare A6-EC motors at slave positions 0..5 stand in for J1..J6, so the drive-side gear ratios of the definition (100/100/100/18/100/10) are written to bare motors and one joint revolution is that many motor revolutions. Derived 2026-09-15 from config/bench-ninemotor-a6ec.json (axes J1..J6, bus_bringup, runtime, cycle) with the robot reference changed to robots/rosie_1420_v1.json; limits are the bench-relay v4-derived values narrowed where the 1420 factory URDF is tighter. Bench only: no gearbox, no payload, no brakes; authorises no motion by itself. | bench-tree brakeless override

bus.unknown_slaves_note: Owner direction 2026-09-15: nine bare bench motors are connected on bench-servo; six are used as the Rosie 1420 J1..J6 and the other three may stay connected in PREOP without outputs.
bus.hold_on_robot_note: This bench uses the Rosie 1420 robot definition to exercise its joint scaling on six bare motors. It is not an assembled robot cell; the owner explicitly permits a connected subset on the test bench. Assembled robot cells must use refuse.

axes.coordinate_evidence_mode_note: Drive-side gearing per the 1420 definition, software ratio 1; the definition limits keep travel below one output revolution, so the fast position is absolute within a turn. Bare bench motor: the joint-level limits are bench-relay v4-derived values narrowed to the 1420 factory URDF where tighter; unverified against any mechanism.

drive_speed_limit_motor_rpm_source: Owner decision 2026-09-15: A6M rated speed 3000 rpm, spec sheet and A6M60-400H2B1-M17 / A6M80-1000H2B1-M17 part numbers. One motor revolution is 131072 counts in the drive frame regardless of the electronic gear ratio, so a motor speed cap does not scale with the gear: 0x607F counts/s = drive_speed_limit_motor_rpm / 60 * motor_encoder_counts_per_rev. Independent of the inhibited start-up verification speed bound and software limits.max_velocity.
